description.narrative: Gaza’s entire population of 2.2 million people is in urgent need of humanitarian assistance to meet their critical needs. The humanitarian context was dire even prior to the escalation in October 2023. Since then, according to OCHA Humanitarian Update (30 September 2024), at least 41,615 people have been killed by the conflict to date; over 70% are women and children, and 96,359 people have been injured. According to the UN, at least 1.9 million people (or nine in ten people) across the Gaza Strip have been internally displaced; this includes people who have been repeatedly displaced (some up to 10 times or more). Displaced communities are living in crowded shelters with limited access to food, water, and sanitation facilities. The IPC analysis (June 2024) found that about 2.15 million people across the Gaza Strip (96 percent of the population) face high levels of acute food insecurity classified in IPC Phase 3 or above (crisis or worse) through September 2024, including nearly 495,000 people (22 percentof the population) experiencing catastrophic food insecurity (IPC Phase 5) and 745,000 people (33 percent) facing emergency (IPC Phase 4). There remains a high and sustained risk of Famine across the whole Gaza Strip as long as conflict continues, and humanitarian access is restricted. As the conflict in Gaza persists, gender-based violence (GBV) is increasingly prevalent. Displaced women voice profound fears for their safety and loss of protection amidst the growing presence of armed forces and separation from support networks. Overcrowded shelters, inadequate facilities, and critical shortages exacerbate the situation, leading to a breakdown of coping mechanisms and heightened risks ofGBV, including child protection issues and sexual exploitation. As the rainy season approaches, the already dire living conditions in Gaza will deteriorate further, putting hundreds of thousands of people at heightened risk of additional displacement, asset loss,health hazards, and limited access to essential services

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
